questions.q: What must exist before you can create an Azure SQL Database, per this lab?
options: A logical server — a container for authentication and firewall rules, not a physical machine
A pre-existing Managed Instance
A configured VNet with a dedicated subnet
An on-prem SQL Server instance to migrate from
questions.explain: Azure SQL Database always needs a logical server first; the create flow prompts you to create one inline if you don't have one.

questions.q: Why did the SSMS connection fail until a firewall rule was added, even though the database deployed successfully?
options: Because the database was never actually created despite the Portal saying so
A freshly created logical server rejects every connection by default, including the deploying user's own machine, until an explicit firewall rule allows it
Because SSMS cannot connect to Azure SQL Database under any circumstances
Because SQL authentication is disabled by default on all Azure SQL servers
questions.explain: Deployment succeeding and network access being allowed are two separate concerns — the firewall rule is what this lab adds in Step 2.

questions.q: What query does this lab use to confirm the full chain (Portal deployment, firewall rule, SSMS connection) actually works?
options: A CREATE TABLE statement to build new schema objects
A query against sys.dm_exec_requests
A SELECT returning DB_NAME(), @@SERVERNAME, and SERVERPROPERTY('Edition')
A stored procedure call requiring SQL Server Agent
questions.explain: An edition string containing "SQL Azure" confirms you're really connected to Azure SQL Database, using ordinary SELECT syntax already covered in T-SQL Development.

questions.q: Why does this lab deliberately leave compute and storage at the smallest available tier?
options: Because this lab is about proving connectivity works end to end, not about performance — tier selection is covered later starting in Lesson 8
Because larger tiers cannot be created through the Portal
Because smaller tiers deploy with zero firewall configuration required
Because Azure SQL Database only offers one tier
questions.explain: Lesson 8 onward covers purchasing models, service tiers, and compute options in full — this lab intentionally skips past that decision.

questions.q: What does Chapter 2 pick up immediately after this lab, per the lesson's closing note?
options: The same server/database create flow, now via the Azure CLI, plus the full menu of purchasing models, service tiers, and compute options this lab skipped past
Configuring Always On Availability Groups
A completely unrelated topic with no connection to this lab
Migrating an on-prem database into the environment just built
questions.explain: Chapter 2, "Deploying Azure SQL," starts with creating servers and databases via CLI (Lesson 7) and works through the options this lab used at their smallest setting.
